title: Negative Numbers
description: Understanding, ordering, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing directed numbers, with real-world contexts.

notes.heading: What Are Negative Numbers?
notes.body:
Negative numbers extend the number system below zero. They are essential for describing debts, temperatures below freezing, depths below sea level, and many other real-life situations.

📌 Definition
A negative number is any number less than zero. We write it with a minus sign in front, such as $-3$, $-10$ or $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

    $$\dots, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots$$

🔑 Key Concept
Zero is the boundary between positive and negative numbers. Zero itself is neither positive nor negative. Every positive number has a matching negative number called its opposite; for example, $+5$ and $-5$ are opposites and are the same distance from zero on a number line.

💡 Worked Example — Real-world negatives
Represent each situation with a directed number.

  • 8 degrees below zero  →  $-8^\circ\text{C}$
  • A debt of £20  →  −£20
  • 15 metres below sea level  →  $-15\ \text{m}$
  • 3 floors below ground  →  $-3$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The negative sign tells us direction or position relative to zero
• A number without a sign is understood to be positive
• $-a$ is negative when $a$ is positive, but positive when $a$ is already negative (for example, $-(-4)=4$)
• The number line is the best visual tool for understanding negative numbers

notes.heading: Ordering and Comparing Directed Numbers
notes.body:
Comparing negative numbers correctly is one of the most important skills in this topic. A number line makes the ordering clear.

📌 Definition
To compare two numbers is to decide which is greater. We use the symbols $>$ (greater than) and $<$ (less than).

🔑 How it works
On a number line, numbers increase as you move to the right and decrease as you move to the left.

    $$-7 \quad -6 \quad -5 \quad -4 \quad -3 \quad -2 \quad -1 \quad 0 \quad 1 \quad 2 \quad 3$$

    Any positive number is greater than any negative number.
    When two numbers are negative, the one closer to zero is greater.

💡 Worked Example — Ordering from smallest to largest
Write $-4$, $2$, $-1$, $-6$, $0$ in order from smallest to largest.

  Step 1: Locate each number on a number line
    $-6$ is furthest left, then $-4$, then $-1$, then $0$, then $2$.

  Step 2: Read from left to right
    $$-6 < -4 < -1 < 0 < 2$$

⚠️ Common Misconception
Students often think $-8$ is bigger than $-3$ because 8 is bigger than 3. Remember: for negatives, the larger digit means the number is further from zero and therefore smaller.

✅ Check
Always ask: which number is further to the right on the number line? That number is the greater one.

notes.heading: Adding Positive and Negative Numbers
notes.body:
Addition with negatives follows a simple movement rule on the number line. Learning the rule saves time and avoids counting mistakes.

📌 Definition
Adding a positive number means moving to the right on the number line. Adding a negative number means moving to the left.

🔑 Key Concept
Use these two rules for addition:

    Positive + Positive = Positive
    Negative + Negative = Negative (add the digits, keep the minus sign)
    Positive + Negative = Subtract the smaller digit from the larger digit and keep the sign of the larger digit

💡 Worked Example 1 — Adding two negatives
Calculate $-5 + (-7)$.

  Step 1: Adding $-7$ means moving 7 places left from $-5$
  Step 2: $-5 - 7 = -12$

    $$-5 + (-7) = -12$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Adding a positive and a negative
Calculate $8 + (-5)$.

  Step 1: Adding $-5$ is the same as subtracting 5
  Step 2: $8 - 5 = 3$

    $$8 + (-5) = 3$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — Adding a negative to a negative
Calculate $-4 + 9$.

  Step 1: Start at $-4$ and move 9 places right
  Step 2: $-4 + 9 = 5$

    $$-4 + 9 = 5$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Do not simply add the digits when signs are different. $-4 + 9$ is not $-13$; the signs are different, so you subtract the digits and keep the sign of the larger digit.

notes.heading: Subtracting Negative Numbers
notes.body:
Subtracting a negative number is the most confusing operation at first, but it follows a clear pattern: two minus signs make a plus.

📌 Definition
Subtracting a negative number is equivalent to adding its opposite.

    $$a - (-b) = a + b$$

🔑 Key Concept
Think of a minus sign as meaning "the opposite of". So $-(-3)$ means "the opposite of $-3$", which is $+3$. This is why subtracting a negative becomes adding a positive.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Double negative
Calculate $6 - (-2)$.

  Step 1: Two minus signs become one plus sign
    $6 - (-2) = 6 + 2$
  Step 2: Add
    $6 + 2 = 8$

    $$6 - (-2) = 8$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Subtracting from a negative
Calculate $-3 - (-8)$.

  Step 1: Change the double negative to a plus
    $-3 - (-8) = -3 + 8$
  Step 2: Count up from $-3$ by 8
    $-3 + 8 = 5$

    $$-3 - (-8) = 5$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $a + (-b) = a - b$ (adding a negative is subtracting)
• $a - (-b) = a + b$ (subtracting a negative is adding)
• When signs are different and next to each other, they simplify using the double-negative rule
• Use brackets around negative numbers to keep signs clear, especially in calculations

✅ Tip
Rewrite the expression first by simplifying any double signs, then follow the normal addition rules.

notes.heading: Multiplying Negative Numbers
notes.body:
Multiplication of directed numbers follows sign rules that come from repeated addition and patterns. Understanding why the rules work helps you remember them.

📌 Definition
The sign of a product depends on the signs of the numbers being multiplied.

🔑 Key Concept
    Same signs  →  Positive product
    Different signs  →  Negative product

    $$\begin{aligned}
    (+) \times (+) &= (+) \
    (-) \times (-) &= (+) \
    (+) \times (-) &= (-) \
    (-) \times (+) &= (-)
    \end{aligned}$$

Why does $(-) \times (-) = (+)$? Think of $-3 \times (-4)$ as "the opposite of 3 groups of $-4$". Three groups of $-4$ is $-12$, and the opposite of that is $+12$.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Same signs
Calculate $(-5) \times (-6)$.

  Step 1: Same signs, so the answer is positive
  Step 2: $5 \times 6 = 30$

    $$(-5) \times (-6) = 30$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Different signs
Calculate $7 \times (-4)$.

  Step 1: Different signs, so the answer is negative
  Step 2: $7 \times 4 = 28$

    $$7 \times (-4) = -28$$

⚠️ Common Misconception
A negative times a negative is positive, not negative. This is the rule students forget most often. You can check with a pattern: $(-3) \times 2 = -6$, $(-3) \times 1 = -3$, $(-3) \times 0 = 0$, so $(-3) \times (-1) = 3$.

notes.heading: Dividing Negative Numbers
notes.body:
The sign rules for division are exactly the same as for multiplication, because division is the inverse of multiplication.

📌 Definition
Dividing two directed numbers: divide the digits as usual, then apply the sign rule.

🔑 Key Concept
    Same signs  →  Positive quotient
    Different signs  →  Negative quotient

    $$\begin{aligned}
    (+) \div (+) &= (+) \
    (-) \div (-) &= (+) \
    (+) \div (-) &= (-) \
    (-) \div (+) &= (-)
    \end{aligned}$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Same signs
Calculate $(-42) \div (-7)$.

  Step 1: Same signs give a positive answer
  Step 2: $42 \div 7 = 6$

    $$(-42) \div (-7) = 6$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Different signs
Calculate $56 \div (-8)$.

  Step 1: Different signs give a negative answer
  Step 2: $56 \div 8 = 7$

    $$56 \div (-8) = -7$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Division by zero is never allowed
• The sign rules for division match the sign rules for multiplication
• You can always check a division by multiplying the answer by the divisor

✅ Check
For $(-42) \div (-7) = 6$, check: $(-7) \times 6 = -42$. The check works, so the sign is correct.

notes.heading: Mixed Calculations and Real-World Problems
notes.body:
Most exam questions combine several operations or place negative numbers in a real-world context. Work carefully, one step at a time, and use the sign rules you have learned.

📌 Definition
A mixed calculation contains more than one operation with directed numbers. Use the order of operations (BIDMAS/BODMAS): Brackets, Indices, Division and Multiplication (left to right), Addition and Subtraction (left to right).

🔑 How it works
When a calculation contains negative numbers, handle the signs before you calculate:

    1. Simplify any double signs
    2. Work inside brackets first
    3. Do multiplication and division from left to right
    4. Do addition and subtraction from left to right

💡 Worked Example 1 — Mixed calculation
Calculate $-3 + (-4) \times 2$.

  Step 1: Multiplication before addition
    $(-4) \times 2 = -8$
  Step 2: Add
    $-3 + (-8) = -3 - 8 = -11$

    $$-3 + (-4) \times 2 = -11$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Temperature change
At 6 am the temperature was $-5^\circ\text{C}$. By midday it had risen by $8^\circ\text{C}$, then by midnight it had fallen by $12^\circ\text{C}$. What was the midnight temperature?

  Step 1: Write the calculation
    $-5 + 8 - 12$
  Step 2: Work left to right
    $-5 + 8 = 3$
    $3 - 12 = -9$

    The midnight temperature was $-9^\circ\text{C}$.

💡 Worked Example 3 — Bank balance
Maya's bank balance is −＄25. She deposits ＄40, then withdraws ＄85. What is her new balance?

  Step 1: Write the calculation
    $-25 + 40 - 85$
  Step 2: Work left to right
    $-25 + 40 = 15$
    $15 - 85 = -70$

    Maya's new balance is −＄70.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Ignoring the order of operations. In $-3 + (-4) \times 2$, you must multiply before adding. A common wrong answer is $-14$, from adding first then multiplying.

✅ Tip
Write each step on a new line and keep the signs with the numbers. This makes it much harder to lose a minus sign.

flashcards.definition: A number less than zero, written with a minus sign.
A number with a direction: positive or negative.
flashcards.example: $+5$ and $-5$ are directed numbers with opposite directions.

flashcards.definition: A straight line showing numbers in order; numbers increase to the right.
flashcards.example: $-3 < -1$ because $-3$ is to the left of $-1$ on the number line.

flashcards.definition: The first number is smaller than the second number.
flashcards.example: $-8 < -3$ because $-8$ is further from zero in the negative direction.

flashcards.definition: The first number is larger than the second number.
Two minus signs next to each other simplify to a plus sign.
Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting the positive number.
Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the positive number.
Multiplying or dividing two numbers with the same sign gives a positive answer.
Multiplying or dividing two numbers with different signs gives a negative answer.
An even number of negative factors gives a positive product; an odd number gives a negative product.
Simplify double signs and brackets first, then multiply/divide, then add/subtract.

questions.explanation: $-4$ is closer to zero than $-9$, so it is greater. On a number line, $-4$ lies to the right of $-9$.

questions.stem: Put these in order from smallest to largest: $-3$, $2$, $-7$, $0$, $-1$.
questions.explanation: On a number line, reading from left to right gives $-7, -3, -1, 0, 2$, which is smallest to largest.
Starting at $-6$ and moving 4 places to the right lands on $-2$. The signs are different, so subtract the digits and keep the sign of the larger digit.
Adding $-8$ is the same as subtracting 8. Starting at $-5$ and moving 8 places left gives $-13$.
Two minus signs make a plus, so $7 - (-3) = 7 + 3 = 10$.
Subtracting 9 from $-4$ means moving 9 places left on the number line: $-4 - 9 = -13$.
The signs are different, so the answer is negative. $6 \times 5 = 30$, therefore $(-6) \times 5 = -30$.
The signs are the same, so the answer is positive. $7 \times 3 = 21$, therefore $(-7) \times (-3) = 21$.
Same signs give a positive answer. $48 \div 6 = 8$, so $(-48) \div (-6) = 8$.
Different signs give a negative answer. $36 \div 9 = 4$, so $36 \div (-9) = -4$.
Without brackets, the power applies only to the 3, so $-3^2 = -(3 \times 3) = -9$. The same is true of $-(3)^2$. Note that $(-3)^2 = 9$ because the brackets make the negative part of the base.

questions.stem: The temperature at midnight was $-8^\circ\text{C}$. By 10 am it had risen by $13^\circ\text{C}$. What was the temperature at 10 am?
questions.explanation: Risen means add. $-8 + 13 = 5$, so the temperature at 10 am was $5^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.stem: A submarine is at $-45$ metres. It dives another $28$ metres. What is its new depth?
questions.explanation: Diving deeper means moving further below sea level, so add $-28$. $-45 + (-28) = -73$, so the submarine is at $-73$ metres.

questions.stem: A bank account starts with a balance of −＄50. The owner deposits ＄120, then withdraws ＄85. What is the final balance?
questions.explanation: Depositing adds money and withdrawing subtracts money: $-50 + 120 - 85$. Working left to right, $-50 + 120 = 70$, then $70 - 85 = -15$. The final balance is −＄15.
